title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The identities X_1⊗X_2 ≃ Hom(X_1^∨,X_2) and the existence of a dual topos X^∨ only make sense for 'dualizable' topoi: presheaf topoi, or more generally exponentiable/continuous ones. They are stated without any hypothesis; his own '𝓕(X^∨)?' shows he was aware this is open.

In the last two lines the target ∏_{J^+}𝓕(X_{I_j}) is a product of categories. A functor preserving colimits multi-variably should land in the tensor product ⊗_{J^+}𝓕(X_{I_j}) = 𝓕(X_{∐_{J^+} I_j}), not in the cartesian product. As written the formula is only correct for |J^+| = 1 (or if ∏ is read as ⊗).
'≃ Hom(𝓕(X_1)°,𝓕(X_2)°;Ens)' without decorations drops the limit-preservation condition, presumably a shorthand.

For general topoi, 𝓕(X)^∨ needs a size-controlled definition, e.g. colimit-preserving functors 𝓕(X)→Ens or the Pr^L dual. Hom(𝓕(X),Ens) is not small-generated, and the page does not specify which is meant.

ideas.what: Isbell conjugation pair and the coend/contraction pairing A^∧ × A^∨ → Ens, giving A^∧ ≃ cocontinuous functors on A^∨ (previous page, used here)
ideas.modern_name: Isbell duality; presheaf categories as mutually dual objects in Pr^L via the coend pairing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Isbell (1960/66), Lawvere; dualizability in Pr^L made explicit by Lurie (Higher Algebra)
ideas.where_published: Tensor product of functors in SGA4 Exp. I; the duality as such is not in a published text as far as I know

ideas.what: Sheaves on a product topos as functors limit-preserving in each variable, 𝓕(X_1×X_2) ≃ Hom^!(𝓕(X_1)°,𝓕(X_2))
ideas.modern_name: Sh(X×Y) ≃ Sh(X)⊗Sh(Y) in Pr^L, with C⊗D ≃ Fun^R(C^op,D)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pitts (1985, product of toposes vs tensor of cocomplete categories); Lurie (HA 4.8.1, HTT 7.3.3 for ∞-topoi)

ideas.what: Duality of topoi X ↦ X^∨ with X_1⊗X_2 ≃ Hom(X_1^∨,X_2): a closed / compact-closed-type structure on topoi
ideas.modern_name: Dualizable objects of Pr^L; exponentiable topoi (continuous sheaf categories); compactly assembled categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Johnstone–Joyal 1982 (continuous categories and exponentiable toposes); Lurie; Efimov (dualizable categories)

ideas.what: Mixed-variance multi-correspondences: partition J = J^+ ⊔ J^- of the factors into inputs and outputs, with 𝓕(X_I) read as multi-functors from the inputs to the outputs
ideas.modern_name: Polycategorical / compact-closed calculus of profunctors (distributeurs) and multi-variable adjunctions

ideas.what: Top(A) := Ens^A with geometric morphisms Top(A) → X ↔ functors A → Pt(X)
ideas.modern_name: Copresheaf topos as free topos on A-indexed diagrams of points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in topos theory (pointwise flatness; e.g. Johnstone, Elephant)
ideas.where_published: Ingredients in SGA4 (points of topoi, flat functors)

missed.claim: Grothendieck writes the sheaf category of a product topos as limit-preserving functors 𝓕(X_1)° → 𝓕(X_2), i.e. as the Lurie/Pitts tensor product of presentable categories. He embeds this in a duality X ↦ X^∨ with X_1⊗X_2 ≃ Hom(X_1^∨,X_2). This anticipates, independently and around 1982, the Pr^L-dualizability viewpoint on topoi now central in higher topos theory and in the theory of dualizable/compactly assembled categories.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority/context rather than new mathematics. The results are now known (Pitts 1985, Johnstone–Joyal 1982, Lurie). It shows Grothendieck framing topoi as dualizable objects in a monoidal 2-category of cocomplete categories, which links to Efimov's dualizable categories and to 'six-functor' formalisms built from correspondences.

missed.claim: He sets up a systematic multi-variable signed calculus (J = J^+ ⊔ J^-) for correspondences between topoi, and asks what the dual topos X^∨ is in general. He leaves open which topoi have a dual, and what 𝓕(X^∨) is when X is not a presheaf topos.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The answer (dualizability ⇔ continuity/exponentiability; Johnstone–Joyal, and in ∞-categories compact assembly) exists. The polycategorical packaging of topos correspondences with explicit input/output signs is not standard and could organise 'topos-theoretic correspondences' à la six functors.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches, apparently around or after 1982, a duality/tensor calculus for topoi whose central formula is the modern Pr^L tensor product of sheaf categories, with a dual topos X^∨. This is a nice anticipation of Pitts and of Lurie's viewpoint, contemporaneous with Johnstone–Joyal. But it is a sketch with gaps (dualizability hypotheses, products vs tensors), and the results themselves are now well established.
transcription_corrections: Top left: '(∏_{i∈I} A_i)^∧' (index i, not j).
Line 3: '𝓕(𝒳_1×…×𝒳_n) ≃ [functors] A_1°×…×A_n° → Ens'; the struck symbol is '≃' and 'E' is 'Ens'.
Bottom left: 'X ⇉ Y' with arrows f, g; its dual is 'X̌ ⇉ Y̌' with arrows f^∨ and g^∨ (not φ^∨).
Second-to-last bracket line: the domain is most likely ∏_{j∈J^-} 𝓕(X_{I_j}) (index set J^-); 'I_j^-' is a misreading.
'X_I = ∏_{i∈I} X_i': the superscript above ∏ is unclear ('bm' in the transcription), possibly 'fin' or a struck-out word.
'𝓕(X_J) 𝓕(X_J^∨)' and 'X_J^∧ X_J^∨': the first symbol may be 'X_J' rather than 'X_J^∧'.
Bottom right: 'F ∈ 𝓕(Top(A)) = A^∨' and 'G ∈ Ob B^∨'.
